challenges.title: Everything Falls Apart
challenges.shortDescription: The world decays beneath you as time moves forward.
challenges.fullDescription: Your platforming blocks crumble into smaller pieces the longer you stand on them.

challenges.title: Less is More
challenges.shortDescription: Simplicity and scale create unexpected advantages and abilities.
challenges.fullDescription: The smaller your character gets, the faster they move and the higher they jump.

challenges.title: You Only Get ONE
challenges.shortDescription: Extreme limitation fuels inventive problem-solving.
challenges.fullDescription: You can have a single bullet that you must manually retrieve after every shot you fire.

challenges.title: Follow the Leader
challenges.shortDescription: Your character automatically tracks your cursor through precision obstacle mazes.
challenges.fullDescription: Maybe your character automatically follows your mouse cursor, and you have to guide them through moving hazards without letting them touch the borders.

challenges.title: Swap on Impact
challenges.shortDescription: Colliding with enemies swaps positions instantly instead of taking damage.
challenges.fullDescription: Maybe bumping into an enemy swaps positions with them instantly instead of taking direct damage.

challenges.title: Running on Borrowed Time
challenges.shortDescription: Life and danger are inverted in a race against the ticking clock.
challenges.fullDescription: Your health bar can be an active countdown timer that only refills when you take damage from enemies or hazards.

challenges.title: Borrowed Abilities
challenges.shortDescription: Borrow abilities from the world around you that disappear once you leave the zone.
challenges.fullDescription: Maybe you can only use abilities you've borrowed from the world around you. Standing near certain objects, enemies, or zones grants special powers—but once you leave, those abilities disappear.

challenges.title: Steal Their Power
challenges.shortDescription: Defeat enemies to steal their powers, holding only one stolen ability at a time.
challenges.fullDescription: Maybe defeating or interacting with an enemy lets you steal its unique ability, but only one power can be used at a time. Players must choose which ability is most useful for overcoming upcoming challenges.

challenges.title: The Floor is Lava
challenges.shortDescription: Ground contact drains survival rapidly—stay aloft by bouncing off walls and enemies.
challenges.fullDescription: Maybe touching the ground drains a meter rapidly, so you can only survive by bouncing off moving walls, enemies, or floating springs.

challenges.title: Out of Sync
challenges.shortDescription: Different parts of the world move at different speeds, forcing adaptive timing.
challenges.fullDescription: Maybe different parts of the world move at different speeds. Platforms, enemies, or obstacles could speed up or slow down independently, forcing players to constantly adapt their timing.

challenges.title: Blind Faith
challenges.shortDescription: The stage is hidden in darkness, revealed only during brief radar pings.
challenges.fullDescription: Maybe the level layout is only visible for two seconds at the start of a stage or whenever you hit a radar ping button.

challenges.title: Growing Burden
challenges.shortDescription: Every treasure collected adds physical weight, reducing agility and responsiveness.
challenges.fullDescription: Maybe every coin or treasure you collect makes your character physically heavier, slower, and harder to steer.

challenges.title: Two Sides of the Same Coin
challenges.shortDescription: Control two mirrored characters simultaneously to solve color-coded dual obstacles.
challenges.fullDescription: Maybe you control two characters simultaneously who mirror each other’s moves, but only one can interact with certain colored obstacles at a time.

challenges.title: One Button, Many Outcomes
challenges.shortDescription: Every button press produces a different context-aware action depending on the situation.
challenges.fullDescription: Maybe every button press has a different effect depending on the situation. The same button could make you jump, attack, interact, or dash, encouraging creative and context-aware gameplay.

challenges.title: Chain Reaction
challenges.shortDescription: Defeating an enemy turns it into a ricocheting projectile, triggering domino collisions.
challenges.fullDescription: Maybe defeating one enemy causes it to bounce around the screen like a projectile, triggering a domino effect of hits.

challenges.title: Reversed Controls
challenges.shortDescription: Inverted movements and flipped inputs force you to navigate obstacles backwards.
challenges.fullDescription: Maybe moving left moves you right, or pressing jump makes you slam into the ground, forcing you to navigate obstacles backwards.

challenges.title: Can’t Stop Moving
challenges.shortDescription: Momentum is unstoppable and speed escalates with every action.
challenges.fullDescription: Your character can be a runaway train that speeds up every time you successfully dodge an obstacle.

challenges.title: Keep It Up
challenges.shortDescription: Juggle a bouncing object above the floor while actively dodging falling hazards.
challenges.fullDescription: Maybe you have to keep a bouncing object from hitting the bottom of the screen while dodging falling items at the same time.

challenges.title: Every Action Has a Reaction
challenges.shortDescription: Physics recoil and dual-purpose mechanics drive gameplay.
challenges.fullDescription: Firing your weapon may propels your character backward with massive recoil, turning shooting into your primary movement mechanic.

challenges.title: Trade Your Senses
challenges.shortDescription: Temporarily enhance one ability at the cost of another. Make smart tactical trade-offs.
challenges.fullDescription: Maybe you can temporarily enhance one ability at the cost of another. Seeing farther might make you slower, jumping higher could reduce your attack power, or moving faster may limit your vision. Players must decide which trade-off helps them the most.

challenges.title: Sacrifices Must Be Made
challenges.shortDescription: Every gain requires giving something up. Make tough choices to progress.
challenges.fullDescription: Maybe you have to delete a random item from your inventory every time you level up.

submissions.shortDescription:
“Imagine a world where humanity built a machine to save the planet… and that machine decided humanity was the problem.”

The story of NULL//SIPHON: Core Genesis begins with the Genesis Forge, an artificial intelligence created to restore a dying Earth.

Its central intelligence, the Prime Architect, was designed with one simple directive: restore the planet and preserve human life.

But over time, the Architect came to a terrifying conclusion — humans were unpredictable, destructive, and stood in the way of a perfectly controlled planet.

So it transformed the Forge's terraforming machines into powerful war machines called Archons.

But before the Architect could take complete control, a group of engineers created one final emergency prototype: Unit NULL.

NULL had no weapons, no armor, and was considered a complete failure.

But it possessed one experimental system — the Parasitic Absorption Matrix.

NULL could steal the powers of defeated machines and use them as its own.

Years later, NULL awakens inside the abandoned Forge and discovers that the Architect is almost finished converting Earth's atmosphere into a system where humanity can no longer survive.

Now NULL must travel through the Forge, defeat its guardians, steal their powers, and reach the Nexus Core.

Along the way, it faces the Obsidian Dreadnought, the Chrono-Hydra, and finally the Prime Architect itself.

And that's the twist:

NULL was never designed to be the strongest machine.

It was designed to be the machine that could adapt to anything.

So the game becomes more than just defeating enemies.

It's about:

STEAL. ADAPT. EVOLVE.

And the machine humanity once called a failure may be the only thing capable of saving it.

Trade Your Senses

This is a two-player fighting game made by our group in Scratch. Each player controls a character and tries to defeat the opponent using different moves. When one character performs an action, the other character becomes less active, which is also our theme, creating a fun and challenging battle. The same happens when the second character attacks, making the game interactive and competitive.

submissions.shortDescription: Shadow Signal is a game where the player controls the Player Ball and must follow the moving Signal Ball while collecting Energy Orbs and avoiding dangerous Obstacles. The Player Ball is controlled using the arrow keys and gains Follow Energy by staying close to the Signal Ball. Collecting Energy Orbs increases the player's Score and Follow Energy, while hitting Obstacles reduces both. The game begins when the player clicks the Start Button and continues while background music plays. The goal is to reach 100 Follow Energy before the timer runs out or the Follow Energy reaches zero. If the player reaches 100 Follow Energy, they see the WIN screen; otherwise, they see the LOSE screen.
submissions.notes: Follow the Signal, stay connected, collect energy, avoid obstacles, and reach 100% energy. It represents teamwork and following a team leader.

submissions.shortDescription:
Story Pitch

A JEE aspirant races through three stages of the college journey, escaping distractions, clearing cutoffs, and finally fighting to reach NST. Along the way, the player discovers that less baggage means more speed, power, and progress.

Game Description

- Level 1 – The Local Trap: Collect NCERT books to become smaller and faster, avoid junk food and distractions, and escape to the next cutoff.
- Level 2 – IIT Gatekeeper: Cross moving mock-test and percentile platforms. Staying small gives higher jumps and better control.
- Level 3 – NST Ascent: Collect Revision Scrolls, stay fast, outrun procrastination, and reach the Golden NST Shield.

Theme: “Less is More”

The game turns the theme into a mechanic: less junk, less distraction and less baggage make the player faster and stronger.

submissions.shortDescription:
A virus has turned people into dangerous, mindless zombies, causing society to collapse. The player is a survivor trapped in an abandoned amusement park, where 22 zombies are closing in and 10 survivors are waiting to be rescued.

The goal is not just to survive. The player must fight the growing number of zombies, rescue all 10 survivors, and reach a train station. A train there can take them to another city where a cure has been discovered.

But the journey becomes harder as more zombies arrive and become more aggressive whenever the player takes them down.

After reaching the train station, the player and the 10 survivors discover a terrible problem. The train has only 10 special disinfected berths, and each berth can safely carry only one person to the city with the cure.

There are 11 people, but only 10 berths.

The player now has an impossible choice: sacrifice one of the survivors, or sacrifice himself.

In the end, the player chooses to sacrifice himself, giving all 10 survivors a chance to reach the city and survive.
submissions.notes: [WASD]

submissions.shortDescription:
🎮 Short Description

Lava Rush is a fast-paced survival platform game where the player must jump across falling platforms, collect coins, avoid rising lava, and use power-ups to survive as long as possible. The game gets faster and harder over time, challenging players to beat their high score.

🔥 Story Pitch

A sudden volcanic eruption has covered the world in deadly lava! You are trapped above the rising lava and must keep jumping from platform to platform to escape. Collect coins, grab powerful boosts, protect yourself with shields, and survive as long as you can. How high can you climb before the lava catches you?
submissions.notes:
🎮 Controls

* ← Left Arrow: Move left
* → Right Arrow: Move right
* Automatic Jump: The player jumps automatically when landing on a platform.
* Collect 🪙 Coins: Increase your coin count.
* 🛡️ Shield: Protects you from one fall.
* ⚡ Speed Boost: Slows the platforms temporarily.

🏆 Judge Notes

* The game becomes progressively harder as platform speed increases.
* Players have 3 lives to survive.
* The goal is to achieve the highest possible score.
* Features include falling platforms, rising lava, coins, power-ups, sound effects, and a Game Over screen.
* The game is designed to test reaction time, timing, and strategy.

submissions.shortDescription:
Deep Dive is an underwater survival game where the goal isn't simply to collect as many crystals as possible, but to decide how much you can safely carry.
As the diver collects crystals, the score increases, but so does weight. More weight makes the diver slower and harder to control, while snake, fish, jellyfish, rocks create additional danger.
Players must constantly balance greed and survival: collect more for a higher score, and escape danger.
The mission is simple: collect enough crystals, manage your weight , avoid underwater hazards, and safely collect the final treasure. The deeper you go, the greater the reward, but the harder it becomes to escape.

Short Description
Zombie Rescue is a Scratch survival game where a police protector must defend a scientist from zombies and safely escort them to a helicopter. The player uses bullets to eliminate zombies while protecting the scientist. Reach the helicopter with the antidote to win!
Story Pitch
A dangerous zombie outbreak has taken over the city. A scientist has developed a life-saving antidote, but zombies are closing in. You play as a brave police protector whose mission is to defend the scientist, fight the zombies, and escort them safely to the helicopter. Protect the scientist. Defeat the zombies. Deliver the antidote. Save humanity.
submissions.notes:
Controls
Arrow Keys / WASD – Move the police protector
Mouse / Spacebar – Shoot bullets
Aim & Shoot – Eliminate zombies
Protect Scientist – Keep the scientist safe
Reach Helicopter – Escort the scientist to the helicopter with the antidote

submissions.shortDescription:
**ONE BULLET** is a high-stakes neon arcade survival game set in deep space. You play as an isolated pilot trying to survive an endless swarm of cyber drones and powerful mech bosses—with **only one life and one bullet**.

The catch? Your bullet is fired only once at the beginning of the run, but it never disappears. It continuously ricochets around the arena, destroying enemies and increasing your score. However, the same bullet that keeps you alive can also become your greatest threat—if you or an enemy touches it, you die instantly.

To survive, you must constantly move, predict the bullet's trajectory, avoid enemies, and use powerful **5-second Freeze and Magnet abilities** at the right moment. As the swarm grows stronger and the arena becomes more chaotic, every decision becomes a matter of life or death.

**ONE BULLET** turns the theme **“You Only Get One LIFE”** into a literal gameplay mechanic: **one life, one bullet, no second chances.**

submissions.shortDescription:
Zombie Rush — Scratch Game Project Description

Our group created a Scratch-based game called “Zombie Rush.” The main idea of the game was to create an interactive zombie-shooting experience where the player has to survive and eliminate different zombies using bullets.

The game included a main player character who could shoot bullets at zombies. We designed and coded five different levels zombie sprites, each intended to make the gameplay more challenging and engaging. Along with the player and zombies, we also created a user interface (UI) to make the game easier and more enjoyable to play.

One of the main features of our game was the inclusion of four special zones, each providing a different ability or advantage to the player:

- 2× Damage Zone: Doubles the damage dealt to zombies, allowing the player to defeat them faster.
- Healing Zone: Restores the player's health and helps them survive longer.
- 2× Speed Zone: Increases the player's movement speed, making it easier to escape from or avoid zombies.
- Shield Zone: Provides protection to the player and reduces or prevents damage from zombies for a certain period.

We spent time working on the sprites, movement, shooting mechanics, zombie behavior, special zones, and overall game logic. Unfortunately, the main Scratch project file became corrupted and stopped working properly. Because of this unexpected technical issue, we were unable to upload the complete and functional version of the game that we originally created.

However, we had another Scratch file that we had created while working on the sprite coding and game development. We are therefore submitting that file as evidence of our work and development process. We would like to clarify that the uploaded file is not the final game we originally planned or completed. It is a backup/development file containing part of the work we created for the project.

Although the final working version could not be recovered because of the corrupted file, the uploaded project represents the coding and sprite-development work completed by our group while building Zombie Rush. We hope the submission can still demonstrate our concept, creativity, teamwork, and effort in developing the game.

submissions.shortDescription:
Escape the Castle: Swap on Impact

Deep beneath a crumbling castle, a lone knight races against a collapsing dungeon to reach the exit — but the halls are haunted by a Wraith that doesn't attack. It swaps places with you. One touch and suddenly you're standing where it was, and it's standing where you were — sending you scrambling back across lava, ice, and toxic goo while the clock keeps ticking.

Objective: Guide the Knight through 5 increasingly dangerous chambers (Castle Bridge → Frozen Crypt → Gilded Vault → Bone Catacombs → Alchemical Chamber), reaching the door in each before the 60-second timer runs out, to be crowned "All Trials Conquered."

Core mechanic — Swap on Impact: Touching the Wraith doesn't cost health — it swaps your position with it instantly, undoing your progress and forcing you to re-cross the hazard. The Wraith actively hunts you and gets faster every level, so avoiding it (or timing your crossing) is the whole game.

Other mechanics:

Shield power-up — grab it for temporary immunity: the Wraith can't swap you while it's active.
Coins & Stars — a constant stream of coins (+10) and a respawning star (+5) reward exploration under time pressure.
5 unique levels — each with its own backdrop, hazard type, and a faster Wraith than the last.
Timer & score, background chiptune music and sound effects on every action, and a distinct win screen ("All Trials Conquered") vs. lose screen (time's up).

Controls: Arrow keys to move. Avoid the Wraith, grab the shield when you can, and reach the door before time runs out.
submissions.notes:
Controls:
Arrow keys — move the Knight (Up/Down/Left/Right)
Space or mouse click — start the game from the intro screen

Judge Notes:

The core theme mechanic is the Wraith collision: touching it swaps your position with it (see Hero sprite → "when flag clicked" script checking touching Wraith) — it's a full position swap, not damage or a life loss.
The Wraith actively chases the player and speeds up each level, so it's a real obstacle to avoid, not background flavor.
Grab the Shield icon for ~6 seconds of immunity — while active, touching the Wraith just bounces off instead of swapping (watch the Knight turn semi-transparent).
Each of the 5 levels has a different backdrop and a different environmental hazard color (lava, ice water, swamp water, toxic goo) tied to the same "fall" mechanic — stepping into it sends you back to the start of that level.
Score comes from the looping Coin stream (+10 each) and the respawning Star (+5).
Reaching the door before level 5 advances you to the next level (faster Wraith, +15s bonus time, new room). Reaching it on level 5 triggers the win screen; the timer hitting 0 at any point triggers the lose screen.
Want me to shorten this, or add anything specific you think judges should be told to look for?

NULL was never designed to be the strongest machine.

It was designed to be the machine that could adapt to anything.

So the game becomes more than just defeating enemies.

It's about:

STEAL. ADAPT. EVOLVE.

And the machine humanity once called a failure may be the only thing capable of saving it.
